reason: The key premises are directly and accurately supported by the cited evidence from PMC10041143 (E1-E3), which explicitly states that strength arises from shear-fault energy fluctuations, identifies HAMs as pinning sites, and describes the transient nature of SRO-enhanced strengthening versus the persistent fluctuation-based resistance. The other cited passages (E4, E5) provide general context on deformation behavior but do not directly support the specific mechanistic premises.
premises: Fluctuations in shear-fault energy, not its average, govern strength in CCAs
Local hard atomic motifs (HAMs) correspond to regions of high fault energy and pin dislocations
Enhanced SRO increases initial fault energy and strengthening, but this subdues after multiple dislocation passages
The basic CRSS in random solid-solution state is dominated by resistance from shear-fault energy fluctuations
Wavy, pinned dislocation configurations are a signature of this mechanism
